notes: MMR-27 semantic compiler policy: it maps source categories to game object kinds and typed pending slots; it creates no Bannerlord objects. Every source kind, hamlet role, hero role and hero status that appears must be listed here, or the compile fails. Hamlets and fortresses carry no names, so village and castle names are synthesized from the core town's name with provenance; names are assigned in source-UID order and an ordinal is added only when two would collide. Name templates may use only their own placeholders, and the ordinal must contain {name} and {n}. A realm with a null sovereign gets a synthesized regent hero. Hero roles map to installed Occupation values that carry hero characters or templates in the installed game; each occupations[] entry names that evidence. The table covers the generator's whole hero role catalogue (FWGC++ generated/content_heroes.cpp kEpithets, 17 roles). A role without a realm uses its withoutRealm occupation: ruin-warden domain holders, realm-less pretenders and founders, and keepers or heresiarchs whose people have no surviving city (heroes.cpp: home and realm are both null) become Wanderers; a Lord role without one is refused. harbourmaster maps to Merchant: the installed game has 14 ShipWright characters, all NavalDLC location characters (shipwright_*, shipyard_worker_*) that are neither heroes nor templates, so ShipWright cannot be a generated hero; naval roles are revisited by MMR-35. Lords join the ruling clan of their realm. Town notables attach to their home city's town (or the realm capital when they have no home); village notables (Headman) attach to the hamlet they are present at (presence.site_kind hamlet), or to their home town when they have none. Wanderers stay unaffiliated. A fortress without a garrison city (the writer's -1/"" sentinel) is owned by the ruling clan of the realm whose culture_id equals the fortress's; the generator writes that sentinel only for player-adopted rows, which carry no culture and are refused anyway. Populations are carried as metadata only; mapping them to prosperity or hearths is MMR-33. Producer limits: an explicit settlement_count request is capped at 24 (generator config.cpp require_int_range), but worlds that infer their own settings place cities by habitat packing (settlement.cpp city_limit), so the compiler requires the producer's own founding report (placed_cities equals the site count, never above target_cities, which founding.cpp keeps within city_limit), fortresses within fortress_count, and land (non-harbour-shaped) hamlets per core within hamlets_per_core (humans.cpp; harbour-shaped hamlets come from fisheries, society.cpp). Player-adopted rows (founded_by) are appended past those limits by the generator and belong to the player faction; they are refused here (MMR-30). Nothing is ever added or dropped.
